page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core via multithreading (2 threads per core). It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and AES.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 3 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC core demonstrates solid single-core capability, registering in the top tier on stress-ng single-core tests (3111.39) and scoring strongly in Geekbench single-core testing (2006.0). Uncached memory bandwidth tests for 256MB blocks reflect average tiers (47.71 GB/sec read and 27.73 GB/sec write), with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 29.27 GB/sec. However, because the instance operates on a single dual-threaded physical core, multithreaded and aggregate throughput benchmarks fall into lower tiers, including multi-core Geekbench (2501.0), PassMark CPU score (3861.67), Redis SET throughput (2.89 million ops/sec), and static web serving (2.73 GB/sec).

Cost efficiency is centered around predictable, dedicated low-core compute with modern instruction set availability. The primary tradeoff is the physical concurrency limit inherent to a 1-core, 2-vCPU configuration. Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is suitable for entry-level microservices, development environments, lightweight backend services, small-scale web servers, and single-threaded or low-concurrency applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Based on 1 physical core with 2 threads, it includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports modern extensions such as AVX-512 and AES. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, though overall multithreaded capacity and aggregate I/O throughput remain limited by the single physical core footprint. It provides a balanced compute-to-memory configuration suitable for lightweight enterprise applications, low-concurrency microservices, and development environments requiring consistent single-thread execution.
